65-130.r: International Year of Camelids, 2024 → declared by the United Nations (UN).

65-137.h: Only person with two unshared Nobels: Chemistry + Peace.

65-138.r: Landmine detection → honey bee (genus Apis), a social insect.

65-139.r: Honey bee average flying speed → 16 km/h is the closest option (book: about 15 miles/hour, slower when returning with food).

65-140.r: Honey-bee hive members recognise each other → by smell (hive odour); food location is told by circle and waggle dances.

65-141.r: Waggle dance (figure-eight) → honeybees, to tell hive-mates the direction and distance of food, water or a new nest site.

65-142.r: Deciphering the language of bees (waggle dance) → Karl von Frisch, German-Austrian ethologist; Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1973.

65-144.r: Silica gel pouch in medicine bottles → desiccant that absorbs moisture (controls humidity), does not kill germs.

65-145.r: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize → outstanding contribution to science (by CSIR); Bhatnagar: first DG of CSIR, 'father of research laboratories', first UGC chairman.

65-146.r: Eye donation → cornea (clear front layer; main focusing surface of the eye) is used.

65-147.r: Dehydration → body loses water and salts, mainly sodium chloride (NaCl).

65-148.r: A dehydrated person should NOT drink sea water; tea, coffee, alcohol are mild diuretics but still add water overall.

65-149.r: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) above about 0.45% can cause death (0.10% = 0.10 g per 100 ml blood). The book gives no single answer (*); official key marked 5.0.

65-150.r: Ivan Pavlov (Russian) → experimental psychology: classical conditioning, studied salivating dogs; Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1904.

65-151.r: Men's and women's voices differ (A) because vocal cords differ in length and thickness (R explains A); men's longer, thicker cords → lower pitch.

65-152.r: Women's voice pitch → generally higher than men's (higher frequency, so shriller); pitch depends on frequency.

65-153.r: NOT an indicator of climate change → 'long-term change'. Indicators: floral (plant fossils), cryogenic (glaciation), tectonic (continental drift, pole wandering).

65-155.r: Plants and trees also have life → discovered by Indian scientist Jagadish Chandra Bose.

65-156.r: Cold storage → decomposition of fruits and vegetables is retarded (slowed): low temperature cuts microbe activity but does not kill them.

65-157.r: Pig (omnivore) cannot digest fibre properly; goat, cow and elephant have gut bacteria to digest fibre.
65-157.c: The book calls the elephant a ruminant; it is not (it does not chew cud), though it does digest fibre with gut microbes.
